title: The Preprocessor
description: #include, #define, macros (including parameterized ones), conditional compilation, and include guards.
objectives: Understand what the preprocessor does before real compilation

content.heading: #include and #define
content.body: The preprocessor runs before the compiler proper, performing purely textual transformations on the source based on lines starting with #. #include <file> or #include "file" literally pastes that file's entire contents in at that point, which is how header files share declarations across multiple source files. #define NAME value defines an object-like macro: every subsequent occurrence of NAME in the source is textually replaced with value before compilation — #define PI 3.14159 makes PI usable like a constant, though (unlike const) with no type checking at all, since it's pure text substitution.

content.heading: Parameterized Macros and Conditional Compilation
content.body:
A function-like (parameterized) macro takes arguments: #define SQUARE(x) ((x) * (x)) — the parentheses around x and the whole expression are essential defensive habits, since naive substitution without them can produce surprising results with certain call-site expressions (SQUARE(a + b) without inner parentheses would expand to a + b * a + b, not (a+b)*(a+b)). Because macros are purely textual, they have no real type checking and can behave unexpectedly with expressions that have side effects (like SQUARE(x++), which would increment x twice) — this is a well-known category of macro pitfall, and for simple cases, a real inline function is often safer.

Conditional compilation directives (#if, #ifdef, #ifndef, #else, #endif) let code be selectively included or excluded at compile time, based on whether a macro is defined or a condition evaluates true — used for platform-specific code, debug-only logging, or feature toggles. Include guards, wrapping an entire header file's contents in #ifndef HEADER_NAME / #define HEADER_NAME / ... / #endif, prevent a header's contents from being pasted in more than once if it's (directly or indirectly) included multiple times in the same translation unit, which would otherwise cause duplicate-definition compile errors.

content.explanation: The #ifndef/#define/#endif guard prevents myheader.h's contents from being duplicated if included more than once. LOG expands to an actual printf call only when DEBUG is defined, and to nothing otherwise.

keyPoints: The preprocessor performs purely textual substitution and file inclusion before real compilation
Parenthesize a parameterized macro's parameters and its whole expansion to avoid operator-precedence surprises
Macros have no type checking and can misbehave with argument expressions that have side effects
#ifndef/#define/#endif include guards prevent a header's contents from being duplicated when included multiple times
commonMistakes: Writing a parameterized macro without enough defensive parentheses, causing wrong results at certain call sites
Passing an expression with side effects (like x++) into a macro that references its parameter more than once
Forgetting include guards, causing 'redefinition' compile errors when a header is included from multiple places
